# testdata

Captured artefacts this crate's own tests read. **Not `fixtures/`**: nothing
here is oracle data, and nothing here is an expected value produced by a
reference. These are inputs — recordings of what an older version of *our* code
wrote, kept so a compatibility path can be exercised against the real thing
instead of against a test's idea of it.

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `keystore_v1_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the last build whose encoder wrote format version 1: `Keystore::create` then two `add`s — an imported root `0xB7 * 32` under the tag `0x1A * 20` (v1's `import_with_unverified_tag`, which this crate no longer has) and `F-derive-account-1`. 242 bytes = `22 + 2*94 + 32`. Read by `src/keystore/format.rs`'s version-dispatch test and by `tests/keystore.rs::a_version_1_store_is_refused_with_upgrade_not_damage`; one copy, embedded twice, so the two cannot drift. |
| `keystore_v2_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the last build whose encoder wrote format version 2: `Keystore::create` then two `add`s of the harness's own accounts, `imported_account()` (`F-address-widths`, tag `05ff…800f`) and `derived_account()` (`F-derive-account-1`, tag `4d9b…fbe9`), in the C-free configuration in a scratch worktree. 410 bytes = `22 + 2*178 + 32`; sha256 `590b2083…8520`. The imported record sorts first, so bytes 22..42 are its tag and byte 42 its kind, `1` — which is what `format::older_first_account` reads and what the version refusal names. Read by `src/keystore/format.rs`'s version-dispatch test and by `tests/keystore.rs::the_version_refusal_names_the_refused_stores_first_account_and_how_to_compare_it`; one copy, embedded twice, so the two cannot drift. **A v2 arm built by forging the v1 file's version word would test the forgery**, which is why this file is a capture of what a v2 encoder actually wrote. |
| `keystore_v3_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the format-version-3 encoder **at `Kdf::RECOMMENDED` (65536/3/1)**: `Keystore::create`, `adopt_master`, `add(Account::derive(master, 0))` — what `cli::create::create` writes once the phrase has become a seed — under the fixed password, salt, nonce seed and master that `tests/keystore.rs::a_store_sealed_by_an_earlier_build_opens_and_is_reproduced_byte_for_byte` spells out. 290 bytes = `51 + (45 + 178) + 16`. Captured by an out-of-tree program depending on the crate by path in the C-free configuration (the sealed path never reaches the backend); the test runs in both configurations and requires each to reproduce the bytes. **It is a pin of this build against its own past, not an oracle**: it says nothing about correctness (the RFC 9106 anchor does) and is never re-captured to make a red green — a re-captured file certifies whatever broke it. Re-capture only after a deliberate format change, keeping this file under its own version, which is what happened at version 4: version 4 is what this build writes, this file is kept byte for byte, and its subject is the version-3 READ PATH at the shipped parameter point (arm 1 of the pin test), with the byte-for-byte arm on the v4 pin below. |
| `keystore_v4_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the format-version-4 encoder **at `Kdf::RECOMMENDED` (65536/3/1)**: the same three calls as the v3 pin -- `Keystore::create`, `adopt_master`, `add(Account::derive(master, 0))` -- under the same fixed password, salt, nonce seed and master, by an out-of-tree program depending on the crate by path in the C-free configuration. 307 bytes = `51 + (45 + 195) + 16`; sha256 `828fcf6f…103c`. It is arm 2 of `tests/keystore.rs::a_store_sealed_by_an_earlier_build_opens_and_is_reproduced_byte_for_byte`: this build must reproduce it byte for byte. A pin captured by the build it pins holds nothing until the build moves. Same rule as the v3 pin: never re-captured to make a red green. |
| `keystore_v3_reserved_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the last build whose encoder wrote format version 3, **with a reservation open** and at `Kdf::CHEAP_FOR_TESTS` (8/1/1): `Keystore::create` under the harness's fixed password, salt and nonce seed, `adopt_master` (`F-address-widths`' master, `IMPORTED_MASTER`), `add(Account::derive(master, 0))` (tag `05ff…800f`, `IMPORTED_TAG`), then `persist_advance(&tag, &[0xD1; 32])` -- the two-argument signature of that build -- in a scratch worktree, the way the v2 file was captured. 290 bytes = `51 + (45 + 178) + 16`; sha256 `b4d14a9b…8231`; generation 3, index 1, a reservation at 0, no figures anywhere in it. It is the real file behind the declared-absent arm of the migration: read under Miri by `src/keystore/format.rs`'s version-dispatch test and by its malformation table's `v3_state_2` row (one Argon2 at the cheap point and a derived record, so no WOTS+ generation), and through the public `open` by `tests/keystore.rs::a_version_3_reservation_is_read_with_its_figures_absent_and_still_resigns`, `tests/recon.rs::a_migrated_reservation_declines_to_classify` and `tests/cli.rs::a_migrated_store_says_its_figures_were_not_recorded_and_is_resealed_by_its_first_write`. A captured input of ours, not oracle data; never edited. |
